title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
why_wsp: A Claude Code agent (Claude Opus 5.5) sets the trainable phase masks of a physical optical neural network on an SLM by probing the hardware, forming hypotheses and writing code, replacing per-pixel optimization with a few interpretable optical parameters; motivated explicitly by WSP but the 'weights' are physical, not a digital network's tensors.
domain: optical neural networks / physical hardware (MNIST 0-2 classifier, Fashion-MNIST optical encoder)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code (headless); Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Fable 5.2 in encoder model comparison
target: two SLM phase masks phi1, phi2 'with several hundred thousand pixels in total' (Results); four 434 x 434-pixel SLM regions
interface: code/tensor tools (harness with probe, evaluation and validation tools; CPU-only code; numerical light-propagation models forbidden)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (camera-image measurements, hypothesis per request, notes file as memory)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all phase-mask pixels can change; agent reparametrizes with few parameters, e.g. 'Tuning 13 parameters improves the design' (Fig. 4f)

headline_results.claim: Classifier test accuracy vs gradient-free and backprop
headline_results.quote: our agent reached 91.1% from the task description alone, and 96.8% when it was given the notes and code of an earlier session
they improved the test accuracy from 35% to about 52%
This accuracy matches that of optical weights trained by backpropagation through a calibrated model of the device, 96.3%.
it reached 16.1 dB, against 15.0 dB for PPO and 13.8 dB for the random start

headline_results.claim: Harness ablation on calibrated model: scalar reward only still beats PPO

cost.quote: The budget is 51,200 measurements for the classifier and 25,600 for the encoder
at 0.107 s per measurement or about 1.5 h for the classifier budget, and not by the language model
here about 67,000 camera images, and many hours of training on graphics processors

baselines_and_controls: PPO and policy gradient (settings searched over 22 configurations on calibrated model), backpropagation through calibrated model, start phase masks; harness ablations (no camera images, no probes, no hypotheses, scalar reward only); three Claude models on encoder
runs_and_variance: 'The three classifier runs that received notes or general lessons from earlier sessions reached 89.2%, 91.3% and 96.8% on the test digits (mean 92.4%, standard deviation 3.9 percentage points).' (Methods); encoder 'one run per row' (Fig. 3d); test-set standard error at most 0.9 points
robustness_of_edits: not tested beyond scoring all methods in one interleaved block to control optical drift
verification: statistical (sealed test set scored once); agent-measured optical quantities compared with calibrated model
memorization_vs_reasoning: Reasoning traces show hypothesis-driven probes (tilts, phase steps) and physically interpretable designs (spot router, Fourier router); measured magnifications/astigmatism agree with calibrated model.
limitations_stated: No explicit limitations section; notes runs depend on earlier sessions; few runs per condition; harness ablations done on calibrated model rather than hardware.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab 2026 'Sparks of weight-space programming'
Goworek et al. 2026 Turing replication (arXiv 2611.21449 version)
notes_for_survey: Extends the WSP framing to physical hardware: the agent learns the device by probing and writes optical parameters, so it is closer to agentic experiment design than editing a digital weight tensor. Shows the closed-loop agent beating PPO even with scalar reward only, and that notes passed between sessions gave the largest gain.
